definition.def: Your vision of a future situation or society is what you imagine or hope it would be like, if things were very different from the way they are now.
examples: I have a vision of a society that is free of exploitation and injustice. [+ of]
That's my vision of how the world could be. [+ of]
Turning that vision into a practical reality is not easy.

definition.def: If you have a vision of someone in a particular situation, you imagine them in that situation, for example because you are worried that it might happen, or hope that it will happen.
examples: He had a vision of Cheryl, slumped on a plastic chair in the waiting-room. [+ of]
Maybe you had visions of being surrounded by happy, smiling children. [+ of]

definition.def: A vision is the experience of seeing something that other people cannot see, for example in a religious experience or as a result of madness or taking drugs.
examples: It was on 24th June 1981 that young villagers first reported seeing the Virgin Mary in a vision.

definition.def: Your vision is your ability to see clearly with your eyes.
examples: It causes blindness or serious loss of vision.
In spite of his otherwise excellent vision, he found he was colour-blind.

definition.def: Your vision is everything that you can see from a particular place or position.
examples: Jane blocked Cross's vision and he could see nothing.
I saw other indistinct shapes that stayed out of vision.
